Hi all,

Thanks Alice — sample cXML would be great. I looked through the mapping sheet Priya attached and sketched out what Redwood supports today and recommended fallbacks:

- Required fields (we currently require these for PO ingestion): buyerPartNumber OR supplierPartID, quantity, unitPrice, currency, and a PO number reference.
- Recommended but optional: uom (units of measure), taxCode (we accept a mapped tax code; if missing we can default to the supplier's tax profile), shipTo location (we map to our routing rules).
- Granularity: Redwood supports both single-line and consolidated invoicing. For customers that need consolidated invoicing we provide an invoice grouping key (invoiceGroupId) based on PO header + supplier id. If TruMed requires line-level acceptance acknowledgements, include line numbers (lineOrdinal) in the cXML.
- Tax jurisdictions: we accept a taxJurisdiction field; when absent we will default to supplier profile but will flag mismatches during invoice validation. For PHI or regulated shipments, we recommend passing explicit jurisdiction and taxCode.

Integration notes: for punchout we support standard cXML punches and will translate basket items into our internal line model. For any custom attributes (e.g., buyerExtendedAttribute1) include them as <Extrinsic> tags and we can map server-side.

I attached a filled version of PO-field-mapping-sheet.csv with Redwood9s required/optional flags.

Attachment: PO-field-mapping-sheet.csv (CSV) — Redwood filled mapping.

Priya: Wed 5/26 2pm PT works for the tech portion; I can stay on a short call with legal after.

Thanks,

Alice / team — thanks for the redlines and the collab so far. A few legal positions and proposed edits to accelerate: 

1) Liability cap / PHI carve: we cannot accept an unlimited carve for PHI incidents, but we can offer a two-tiered cap: standard cap of 3x fees capped at $2M; for documented PHI data breach events we9ll raise the cap to 5x fees capped at $5M and include defined remediation SLA obligations (notification timelines, forensics cooperation). I9ve drafted proposed language and attached it to the TruMed_MSA_Redlines_v2.pdf as inline comments.

2) Data segregation / encryption: Redwood will commit to customer-specific KV separation and AES-256 at rest for customer keys; we will note this in a security appendix. We cannot commit to on-prem data residency within the MSA but can reference a Private deployment addendum (separate SOW) if TruMed requires on-prem air-gapped hosting.

3) Order Form / payment terms: regarding net-60, economics team flagged that net-60 materially impacts cashflow for early-stage commitments. We can accept net-45 for initial 12 months with a review clause at renewal, or net-60 with a 2% early-pay discount. Please let us know which is TruMed9s preference and we9ll update the order form.

4) PO acknowledgement SLA: Redwood proposes a 24-hour PO-acknowledgement for EDI/cXML POs; exceptions flagged in 48 hours. If TruMed needs a shorter SLA we should capture it in the Order Form.

Next steps:
- Alice: confirm invoice consolidation preference and whether TruMed will supply a sample cXML (we need one to finalize the mapping).
- Priya / Karthik: get the tech sync notes into the shared doc (I put inline legal comments in the attached PDF).
- Alice: if the two-tier liability cap is acceptable, we can mark the MSA as redlines-complete and move to order form edits.

Attachments: TruMed_MSA_Redlines_v2.pdf (PDF, with Redwood comments), PO-field-mapping-sheet.csv (CSV, Redwood filled)

Proposed follow-up: Fri 5/28 10am PT for a short alignment call (15-20m) to confirm invoice grouping and payment term choice.

Best,
